newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil president's popularity is on the rise-poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazil president's popularity is on the rise-poll.

text.p: Approval ratings for the government of Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso have jumped to 61 percent in November from 49 percent in August, according to a poll published in O Globo newspaper.

The Ibope survey found only 29 percent of the 3,000 people polled disapproved of Cardoso's administration which is seeking to amend the constitution in order to allow the president to run for a second term.

Approval ratings for the government's anti-inflation Real Plan rose as well in November especially among low-income earners. Seventy-nine percent of those polled backed the Real Plan, up from 73 percent in August, and among people earning only up to two minimum salaries 82 percent approved of the Real Plan.

The number of people who have confidence in Cardoso increased to 60 percent in November from 56 percent in August, and the number of people who do not trust the president have fallen to 34 percent from 36 percent.
Cardoso's credibility rating was even higher, at 70 percent, among low income earners of only one minimum salary.
Ibope Executive Director Carlos Augusto Montenegro said the trend was towards growing confidence in the government, O Globo said.

Of the people surveyed, 60 percent said the economy was likely to improve further until March next year, and 42 percent were optimistic about Brazil's future. Sixty-nine percent said they were satisfied with their current living standard.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
